# Burnly v0.1.36

Restores deterministic tray panel placement on Linux Wayland sessions and opens the panel on the monitor whose tray action triggered it.

## Highlights

- **Wayland tray panel placement.** Wayland gives clients no way to place a toplevel window, so the panel opened wherever the compositor decided — typically the middle of the screen — instead of a tray corner. On Linux Wayland sessions where a reachable XWayland display exists, Burnly now selects the GTK X11 backend before GTK initializes (`GDK_BACKEND=x11`), restoring the top-right corner placement. The decision is recorded once per launch as a `platform.display_backend` diagnostic event. Sessions without a usable X display still start normally on native Wayland, where the panel uses compositor placement.
- **The panel opens on the monitor you are using.** Corner placement now prefers the monitor under the pointer, so triggering the tray action on a secondary display opens the panel there instead of on another monitor.

### Manual override

`GDK_BACKEND` keeps working as the manual override in both directions:

```bash
GDK_BACKEND=wayland burnly   # keep native Wayland (compositor placement)
GDK_BACKEND=x11 burnly       # force XWayland positioning
```

See `docs/engineering/known-limitations.md` for the cause, the workaround, and the trigger for removing the XWayland selection.

## Privacy

Burnly continues to read usage-only metadata. It selects model identity, token
counters, and generation timestamps; it never reads prompt text, response
content, tool invocations, project paths, or sensitive credentials.

## Install

### Linux

Run:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://github.com/fikrilal/burnly/releases/latest/download/install-linux.sh | sh
```

For a pinned install of this release:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://github.com/fikrilal/burnly/releases/download/v0.1.36/install-linux.sh | BURNLY_VERSION=v0.1.36 sh
```

### Windows Preview

Download the Windows x64 installer from this release:

```text
burnly-v0.1.36-windows-x86_64.exe
```

The Windows preview installer is not Authenticode-signed. Windows may show an
unknown publisher or SmartScreen warning. Only download Burnly from the
official GitHub release and verify the published `SHA256SUMS`. Tauri updater
artifacts remain cryptographically signed.

### macOS Preview

Run:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://github.com/fikrilal/burnly/releases/latest/download/install-macos.sh | sh
```

For a pinned install of this release:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://github.com/fikrilal/burnly/releases/download/v0.1.36/install-macos.sh | BURNLY_VERSION=v0.1.36 sh
```

Manual `.dmg` installation is also available:

```text
burnly-v0.1.36-macos-aarch64.dmg
burnly-v0.1.36-macos-x86_64.dmg
```

The macOS preview is unsigned and not notarized. If Gatekeeper blocks the
downloaded app, clear quarantine once after copying it to Applications:

```bash
xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Burnly.app
```

## Verification

This release was verified with the full local gates (119 frontend tests, 801 Rust
tests) and with desktop runtime evidence on Ubuntu GNOME Wayland: an isolated
build selected the X11 backend automatically and opened the panel at the
top-right corner of a 3440x1440 monitor (window geometry `440x540+2988+48`, not
the ~`1500,450` screen center), while an opt-out run with `GDK_BACKEND=wayland`
started as a native Wayland client without X windows. Evidence:
`docs/runtime-evidence/2026-10-11-wayland-panel-positioning/`.

Release artifacts include `SHA256SUMS`, GitHub build provenance, signed updater
artifacts, `latest.json`, and the `latest-linux.json` compatibility alias.
